steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Conceptual picture – imagine a big team of clerks who must read a document and then write another one.  
Instead of each clerk reading the text once from left-to-right (like an RNN), every clerk can look at any word at any time and can talk to every other clerk in parallel. That “looking and talking” is the essence of a Transformer.

1. Inputs become vectors  
   • Each token (word, sub-word, etc.) is turned into an embedding vector.  
   • Because order gets lost in a bag of vectors, we add a “positional encoding” (a little wiggle pattern or learned vector) so the model still knows which word sat where.

2. Self-attention: everyone looks at everyone  
   • For every token we form three little views: Query (Q), Key (K), Value (V) by multiplying by learned matrices.  
   • Dot-product(Qᵢ, Kⱼ) says “how much should token i care about token j?”  
   • Softmax turns those scores into weights that sum to 1.  
   • Weighted sum of the V’s gives a new representation for token i that now contains information from all other positions it decided to focus on.  
   • Do this several times in parallel with different learned projections → multi-head attention. Each head can learn a different relation (subject-verb, coreference, etc.).

3. Add & normalize  
   • The new attended vector is added back to the original (residual connection) and run through layer normalization so gradients flow smoothly.

4. Mini-MLP for each position  
   • A position-wise feed-forward neural network (same weights reused at every position) gives the model more non-linear mixing power.

5. Stack layers  
   • Repeat attention + feed-forward + residual + norm blocks a dozen times. Representations become richer the deeper you go.

6. Encoder vs. decoder layouts  
   • Encoder (BERT, first half of original Transformer) lets every position attend to every other in the same sentence. Output is a context-infused embedding per token.  
   • Decoder (second half in translation models like GPT) attends to previous decoded tokens plus the encoder output, but uses a mask so it can’t peek at future words—enabling left-to-right generation.

7. Training objective  
   • Feed in many text pairs and minimize cross-entropy between predicted next token and the real one (language modeling) or between predicted translation and the reference (seq-to-seq). Backprop adjusts all those projection and MLP weights.

8. Inference (generation)  
   • Start with a prompt, compute attention flows, get probabilities for the next token, sample/beam-search, append chosen token, repeat.

Why it works  
   • Attention is content-addressable memory: the model can jump instantly to relevant information no matter how far away in the sequence.  
   • All positions are processed in parallel, so training scales exquisitely on GPUs/TPUs.  
   • Multi-head diversity + deep stacking captures many linguistic patterns without recursion.

So, conceptually, a Transformer is just: “embed tokens → repeatedly let every token ask every other token what it needs to know (self-attention) → mix with small neural networks → (optionally) condition on earlier or external sequences → decode.”
